newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Banco Edwards sees debt upgrade soon.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Banco Edwards sees debt upgrade soon.

text.p: Chile's Banco de A. Edwards expects to be reclassified by bank authorities into the lowest risk category after being downgraded recently following problems with a number of debtors, said CEO Gustavo Favre.
The bank expects the Banking Superintendency to review its books soon and to upgrade the firm into risk category 1, Favre told a news conference.
In July, the authorities slapped a half million dollar fine on the bank and downgraded it into category 2 for breaking legal limits on loans made to failed cemetery company Isacruz.
The bank has not changed its risk evaluation policy as a result of the sanction, but it has carried out internal studies to consider the overall risk of its loan portfolio, he said.
"We want to stress that our loans are well evaluated," said Favre.
"Historically our level of risk has been below the average in the banking sector."
Favre said debts owed by another financially troubled customer, supermarket chain Marmentini, have been completely repaid. But the case of loans made to Isacruz "is rather more complex," he said.
Despite the ongoing problems with Isacruz, the bank does not expect to suffer losses in the long term as the result of loans made to the cemetery company, said Favre.
Bank officials have said that the bank was owed $12.5 million by Isacruz, which collapsed this year with reported debts of $160 million.
Banco Edwards' consumer credit division, Finandes, had also made loans of nearly $20 million to 15,000 Isacruz clients.
Favre, who took over as the bank's chief executive last month, denied speculation that the bank was in talks with Spain's Banco Bilbao de Vizcaya.
"There is nothing (in the speculation)," he said.
Banco Edwards shares climbed in Santiago and New York Tuesday on rumors that the Spanish bank had bought a stake in the Chilean company.
